title: Review: Density; Pressure and hydrostatics; Upthrust / Archimedes' principle; Work done; Kinetic and potential energy; conservation; Work–energy theorem and dissipative forces; Power and efficiency
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: E03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; E03-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; FL02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; FL03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: E01-1#N.9b, E02-1#N.12, E03-1#N.4a, E04-1#N.6b, FL01-1#N.4, FL02-1#N.2, FL03-1#N.7, E01-1#N.5, E02-1#N.4a, E03-1#N.15, E04-1#N.3, FL02-1#N.3. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of doing work, or rate of energy transfer.

items.label: Watt
items.clue: Unit equal to one joule transferred each second.

items.label: Pressure
items.clue: Total perpendicular force divided by area; exists at every place in a gas.

items.label: Archimedes' principle
items.clue: Statement that the upward push from a fluid equals the weight of fluid displaced.

questions.stem: A student carries a bag of weight 15 N up a flight of stairs at constant velocity. The bag moves 4.0 m horizontally and rises 3.0 m, so it travels 5.0 m along the stairs. How much work does the student's upward force do on the bag?

options.text: 60 J, the upward force multiplied by the horizontal distance.
45 J, the upward force multiplied by the height gained.
75 J, the upward force multiplied by the distance along the stairs.
Zero, as the bag moves at constant velocity, so no work is done on it.

questions.explanation: The force is vertical and the displacement is 5.0 m at an angle θ to it, with cos θ = 3.0/5.0. Work = 15 × 5.0 × 0.60 = 45 J: the force times the 3.0 m rise.

questions.stem: Three identical stones are thrown from the top of a sea cliff with the same speed: one straight up, one horizontally and one straight down. Air resistance is negligible. Which stone hits the sea with the greatest speed?

options.text: The one thrown straight down, as its velocity starts in the direction of gravity.
The one thrown upwards, as it falls back from a greater height than the others.
The one thrown horizontally, as it keeps its horizontal speed while gaining vertical speed.
All land at equal speeds: same starting kinetic energy, same drop in height.

questions.explanation: Initial kinetic energy + potential energy lost = final kinetic energy, and both terms are equal for all three stones. The speeds are equal; only the directions and times of flight differ.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides along a level road at a constant speed of 8.0 m s⁻¹. The total resistive force on the cyclist and bicycle is 25 N. What power does the cyclist's driving force develop?
questions.explanation: At constant speed the driving force equals the resistive force, 25 N. P = Fv = 25 × 8.0 = 200 W.

questions.stem: A skier of mass 60 kg starts from rest at the top of a slope and descends through a vertical height of 20 m. At the bottom her speed is 16 m s⁻¹. Take g = 9.81 m s⁻². What is the total work done on the skier by friction and air resistance during the descent?
The density of aluminium is 2.7 g cm⁻³. What is the volume, in m³, of an aluminium block of mass 0.081 kg?
A force of 50 N acts on a flat plate of area 25 cm². The force is at 60° to the plate's surface. What pressure does the force exert on the plate?
questions.explanation: The angle is from the surface, so the perpendicular component is 50 sin 60° = 43.3 N. A = 25 × 10⁻⁴ m², so pressure = 43.3 ÷ 2.5 × 10⁻³ = 1.7 × 10⁴ Pa.

questions.stem: A foam ball of volume V would float, but it is held at rest completely under water by a light string tied to the bottom of a tank. The density of the foam is a quarter of the density ρ of water. Which expression gives the tension in the string?
A worker uses a rope to lower a box straight down at constant speed. Which statement about the work done on the box during the descent is correct?

options.text: The tension does positive work and gravity does negative work on the box.
The tension does negative work and gravity does positive work.
The tension and gravity both do positive work on the box as it moves.
Neither force does any work, as the box's speed does not change.

questions.stem: Object A has mass m and moves at speed 2v. Object B has mass 2m and moves at speed v. What is the kinetic energy of object A divided by the kinetic energy of object B?
questions.explanation: A: ½m(2v)² = 2mv². B: ½(2m)v² = mv². So A has twice B's kinetic energy: doubling the speed multiplies it by 4, doubling the mass only by 2.

questions.stem: Motor A raises a 200 N load through 3.0 m in 6.0 s. Motor B raises a 100 N load through 6.0 m in 4.0 s. Both lift at constant speed. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A develops more power, as it lifts the heavier load.
B does more work, as it lifts its load twice as high.
Both do equal work, and B develops more power.
Both develop equal power, as they do equal work.

questions.explanation: Each does 600 J (200 × 3.0 and 100 × 6.0). B does it in less time: 600 ÷ 4.0 = 150 W against 600 ÷ 6.0 = 100 W.

questions.stem: A child on a toboggan slides across level snow. The child and toboggan have a total mass of 50 kg and slow down from 8.0 m s⁻¹ to 6.0 m s⁻¹. What is the magnitude of the net work done on the child–toboggan system during this time?
A sealed container holds a gas at a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Which statement about this pressure is correct?

options.text: The gas presses mainly on the base of the container, because gas pressure acts downwards.
Pressure is a vector, so the pressures acting on opposite walls of the container cancel out.
The gas exerts a force of 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each wall, whatever the area of that wall.
The gas pushes perpendicular to every wall, exerting 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each square metre of wall.
